newsitem.title: UK: Copper skips higher in late LME, ends above $2,200.
newsitem.headline: Copper skips higher in late LME, ends above $2,200.

text.p: Copper prices pushed higher during Tuesday afternoon LME trading, regaining the $2,200 level to end the session firmer and geared up for Wednesday's Feb option declarations.

Other metals did not fare so well, particularly aluminium which came in for late technical selling, while Monday's star performers nickel and zinc opted for consolidation. Business in the complex was fairly routine throughout the session, traders said.
In copper, the 8,750-tonne stock increase was shrugged off, as inventory rises are being factored in while the current high backwardation persists.
Nearby prompts remain tight, with cash/one day at $22.50 this afternoon, while an influx of borrowing to the Feb date helped arrest a softening trend in premiums and underpin the forward market.
Some resistance was again evident above $2,200, although the close at $2,204, $17 from Monday, was construed constructively on the charts.

Aluminium was unable to make headway above $1,625, despite the 7,500-tonne stock fall, and prices lost ground on late chartist selling. Final business was at $1,617.50, down $8.50, with a test of $1,600/10 likely now.

Nickel prices took a breather, following the sharp run-up seen in recent sessions which culminated in the market hitting 4-1/2 month highs on Monday. The 114-tonne stock increase also cautioned the market, although speculative interest is expected to resume on the upside.
Last trade was at $7,675 a tonne, down just $5 from the overnight kerb close.

Zinc similarly settled for a session of holding fire just under the two-year peaks of Monday, with stiff resistance likely from the mid-$1,170s up to $1,200. A 2,275-tonne stock fall maintained recent trends, and prices ended the LME at $1,169, down $3.
The lead market was relatively unexciting throughout, and a dull kerb ended with three months at a little-changed $674/675 a tonne.
Tin traded routinely, closing at an unchanged $5,855, while alloy ended at an equally steady $1,527/30 a tonne.
